newsitem.title: UK: UK SFO aiding Belgian police insurance fraud probe.
newsitem.headline: UK SFO aiding Belgian police insurance fraud probe.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) confirmed on Sunday that it was helping Belgian authorities in their investigation of a multi-million pound fraud on London's insurance market.

"We are providing assistance to the Belgian authorities. It is one of our mutual legal assistance cases and was started in March," an SFO spokeswoman told Reuters when asked about a report in the Independent on Sunday newspaper.

The newspaper said Belgian police and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) were hunting "for the conspirators behind a network of fraudulent companies that stole tens of millions of pounds from brokers and insurers in London and the U.S. between 1989 and early 1996".

It said there was increasing pressure on the government from British Members of Parliament and from insurance regulators to investigate a Brussels-based group of companies "following mounting evidence that the fraud may have been orchestrated from the UK".
Belgian police would, the paper said, be asking for SFO help in tracing large money transfers from bank accounts in London controlled by the group in question.

The SFO, which declined to comment on any of the named parties in the report, said the arrangement was a usual one under which it could use its powers in Britain on behalf of an overseas fraud investigator.
